basis: Co-authored the memo Solveig Quaresma publicly cited. Her standing in this field is why she is a tier-A route to a foundation that has never heard of us.
Scientific adviser to the Iwasaki Institute since 2021. Reads as a scientist to scientists rather than as a fundraiser.
Known to two family offices through the convening programme. Not a name an endowment committee would recognise.
Screen managers for several endowments, including Fernhollow Umberfield. When they put a name in front of a committee, the committee reads it.
No science standing at all. They are trusted on process and on managers, and on nothing about the field.
Introduced Quaresma to two managers in 2023. She has since asked not to be introduced through him — which is a fact about this target, not about his standing generally.
Adviser on crypto mandates at Gyasi & Ferrante-Obuya and a co-funder on the Lattice SPV. Credible on digital-asset infrastructure and on nothing else.
None. A strong name in the wrong field is a weak route, and this is the case that makes the point.
Trustee of a research charity until December 2023, and speaking at a neurotech conference in November.
A single family office principal. Carries weight with peers of the same size and none above it.
CIO of Fernhollow Umberfield Trust and the first institution to countersign. An endowment CIO vouching to another endowment is the strongest allocator signal available to us.
CIO of a $2B multi-family office that committed to both vehicles inside a year. Has never been asked for anything.
Underwrote the Rails vehicle, so the mandate is real. Not a technologist.
Head of investments at Vetchling Wagtail for three weeks, and an investment director at Greylag Gorsebrook for five years before that. The standing is borrowed from the previous seat.
An analyst placed at Gyasi & Ferrante-Obuya by a conference badge. This row exists to be visibly weak — it is the kind of record that should never carry a route.
